sme_questions.question: Is this how you would state the rule “Order.price_terms”? The wording was sharpened for a reader and awaits your acceptance: Four facts on a sale carry every price and cost. The unit price is the regular, list price of one unit before discount; the net price is the actual selling price of one unit after discount; the unit cost is what one unit cost Contoso; the quantity is how many units. Every amount derives from them: gross is quantity times unit price, net is quantity times net price, cost is quantity times unit cost, discount is gross less net, and margin is net less cost — so margin is profit on the discounted price, not on list. "Unit price" names the regular price, not what was paid.

sme_questions.question: Is this how you would state the rule “Product.price_is_dated”? The wording was sharpened for a reader and awaits your acceptance: A product carries no standing price and no standing cost. A price changes over time, so every price and cost is the one on the sale, dated by the sale, and a product's price is reached through its sales. A product's current price is the regular unit price on its latest sale, stated with that sale's date where it matters. A question qualifying products by price — high-value products — selects products by that price and then counts all their sales, never qualifies individual sale lines.

sme_questions.question: Is this how you would state the rule “Store.channel”? The wording was sharpened for a reader and awaits your acceptance: A store is a shop you can walk into. The online channel is recorded as a store, but a question about stores — how many there are, which ones — covers physical shops only unless it names the online channel. That default holds only when the question is about stores: revenue and every other figure of the sale includes both channels, even when the question's route passes through stores.

sme_questions.question: Is this how you would state the rule “Store.premises_not_place”? The wording was sharpened for a reader and awaits your acceptance: A store is the premises Contoso sells from: a shop standing on one place for one trading period, with its own name, floor area, opening date and closing date. It is part of a location, not the location itself — one place may hold a succession of premises over time, each of them a store. So one store is counted by its premises, and a count or sum over stores is a different question from the same figure over places; an answer that could be read at either level says which level it used.

"How many stores do we have" is a different question and keeps the physical and active defaults.
